interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The postoperative pathology reveals a Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3) diagnosis with pathological stage pT2c. A positive surgical margin finding is noted, which is an adverse factor. Countervailing findings include the absence of extraprostatic extension and no invasion of the seminal vesicles, as documented by "There was no extraprostatic extension; surgical margins were positive; the seminal vesicles were not invaded." The absence of lymph nodes removed means nodal status is not established, and "No nodes sampled; pNx is not pN0." Biopsy findings showed Gleason 3+3 (ISUP grade group 1). Postoperative PSA is not recorded, meaning biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Missing nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding the true extent of disease. Postoperative PSA and its trajectory are crucial information that would revise the prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 68.57 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 41.14–95.99 months; its coverage has not been validated.
